verses.original: Καὶ ἦλθον εἰς τὸ πέραν τῆς θαλάσσης εἰς τὴν χώραν τῶν Γερασηνῶν
verses.transliteration: Kai ēlthon eis to peran tēs thalassēs eis tēn chōran tōn Gerasēnōn
verses.literal: On the other side of the sea they arrived in the region of the Gerasenes
verses.literalPt: Chegaram ao outro lado do mar, ao território dos gerasenos.

verses.original: καὶ ἐξελθόντος αὐτοῦ ἐκ τοῦ πλοίου εὐθὺς ὑπήντησεν αὐτῷ ἐκ τῶν μνημείων ἄνθρωπος ἐν πνεύματι ἀκαθάρτῳ
verses.transliteration: kai exelthontos autou ek tou ploiou euthys hypēntēsen autō ek tōn mnēmeiōn anthrōpos en pneumati akathartō
verses.literal: As soon as . . . Jesus got out of the boat He was met by . . . a man with an unclean spirit who was coming from the tombs
verses.literalPt: Quando Jesus desembarcou, veio logo ao seu encontro, dos túmulos, um homem possesso de espírito imundo,

verses.original: ὃς τὴν κατοίκησιν εἶχεν ἐν τοῖς μνήμασιν καὶ οὐδὲ ἁλύσει οὐκέτι οὐδεὶς ἐδύνατο αὐτὸν δῆσαι
verses.transliteration: hos tēn katoikēsin eichen en tois mnēmasin kai oude halysei ouketi oudeis edynato auton dēsai
verses.literal: This man had been living in the tombs and could no longer be restrained even with chains
verses.literalPt: o qual tinha ali a sua morada, e nem mesmo com cadeias podia já alguém segurá-lo;

verses.original: διὰ τὸ αὐτὸν πολλάκις πέδαις καὶ ἁλύσεσιν δεδέσθαι καὶ διεσπάσθαι ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ τὰς ἁλύσεις καὶ τὰς πέδας συντετρῖφθαι καὶ οὐδεὶς ἴσχυεν αὐτὸν δαμάσαι
verses.transliteration: dia to auton pollakis pedais kai halysesin dedesthai kai diespasthai hyp’ autou tas halyseis kai tas pedas syntetriphthai kai oudeis ischyen auton damasai
verses.literal: Though he was often bound with chains and shackles he had broken . . . . . . the chains and shattered the shackles Now there was no one with the strength to subdue him
verses.literalPt: porque, tendo sido muitas vezes seguro com grilhões e cadeias, tinha quebrado as cadeias e despedaçado os grilhões, e ninguém tinha força para o subjugar;

verses.original: καὶ διὰ παντὸς νυκτὸς καὶ ἡμέρας ἐν τοῖς μνήμασιν καὶ ἐν τοῖς ὄρεσιν ἦν κράζων καὶ κατακόπτων ἑαυτὸν λίθοις
verses.transliteration: kai dia pantos nyktos kai hēmeras en tois mnēmasin kai en tois oresin ēn krazōn kai katakoptōn heauton lithois
verses.literal: Night and day in the tombs and in the mountains he kept crying out and cutting himself with stones
verses.literalPt: e sempre, de dia e de noite, gritava nos túmulos e nos montes, ferindo-se com pedras.

verses.original: Καὶ ἰδὼν τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ἔδραμεν καὶ προσεκύνησεν αὐτόν
verses.transliteration: Kai idōn ton Iēsoun apo makrothen edramen kai prosekynēsen auton
verses.literal: When the man saw Jesus from a distance he ran and fell on his knees before Him
verses.literalPt: Vendo de longe a Jesus, correu para ele e adorou-o,

verses.original: καὶ κράξας φωνῇ μεγάλῃ λέγει Τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί Ἰησοῦ Υἱὲ τοῦ Θεοῦ τοῦ Ὑψίστου ὁρκίζω σε τὸν Θεόν μή με βασανίσῃς
verses.transliteration: kai kraxas phōnē megalē legei Ti emoi kai soi Iēsou Huie tou Theou tou Hypsistou horkizō se ton Theon mē me basanisēs
verses.literal: And he shouted in a loud voice What do You want with me Jesus Son of the Most High God I beg You before God not to torture me
verses.literalPt: gritando em alta voz: Que tenho eu contigo, Jesus, Filho do Deus Altíssimo? Por Deus te conjuro que não me atormentes.

verses.original: ἔλεγεν γὰρ αὐτῷ Ἔξελθε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἀκάθαρτον ἐκ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου
verses.transliteration: elegen gar autō Exelthe to pneuma to akatharton ek tou anthrōpou
verses.literal: For Jesus had already declared . . . Come out of this man you unclean spirit
verses.literalPt: Pois Jesus lhe dissera: Espírito imundo, sai desse homem.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐπηρώτα αὐτόν Τί ὄνομά σοι Καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ Λεγιὼν ὄνομά μοι ὅτι πολλοί ἐσμεν
verses.transliteration: Kai epērōta auton Ti onoma soi Kai legei autō Legiōn onoma moi hoti polloi esmen
verses.literal: What is your name Jesus asked . . . My name is Legion he replied for we are many
verses.literalPt: Perguntou-lhe: Qual é o teu nome? Respondeu ele: Legião é o meu nome, porque somos muitos.

verses.original: καὶ παρεκάλει αὐτὸν πολλὰ ἵνα μὴ αὐτὰ ἀποστείλῃ ἔξω τῆς χώρας
verses.transliteration: kai parekalei auton polla hina mē auta aposteilē exō tēs chōras
verses.literal: And he begged Jesus repeatedly not to send them out of that region
verses.literalPt: E rogava a Jesus, com instância, que os não mandasse para fora do território.

verses.original: Ἦν δὲ ἐκεῖ πρὸς τῷ ὄρει ἀγέλη χοίρων μεγάλη βοσκομένη
verses.transliteration: Ēn de ekei pros tō orei agelē choirōn megalē boskomenē
verses.literal: There on the nearby hillside a large herd of pigs was feeding
verses.literalPt: Pastava ali pelo monte uma grande manada de porcos;

verses.original: καὶ παρεκάλεσαν αὐτὸν λέγοντες Πέμψον ἡμᾶς εἰς τοὺς χοίρους ἵνα εἰς αὐτοὺς εἰσέλθωμεν
verses.transliteration: kai parekalesan auton legontes Pempson hēmas eis tous choirous hina eis autous eiselthōmen
verses.literal: So the demons begged Jesus Send us to the pigs so that we may enter . . . them
verses.literalPt: e os espíritos imundos suplicaram-lhe, dizendo: Envia-nos para os porcos, a fim de que entremos neles.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐπέτρεψεν αὐτοῖς καὶ ἐξελθόντα τὰ πνεύματα τὰ ἀκάθαρτα εἰσῆλθον εἰς τοὺς χοίρους καὶ ὥρμησεν ἡ ἀγέλη κατὰ τοῦ κρημνοῦ εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν ὡς δισχίλιοι καὶ ἐπνίγοντο ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ
verses.transliteration: Kai epetrepsen autois kai exelthonta ta pneumata ta akatharta eisēlthon eis tous choirous kai hōrmēsen hē agelē kata tou krēmnou eis tēn thalassan hōs dischilioi kai epnigonto en tē thalassē
verses.literal: He gave them permission . . . and the unclean spirits came out and went into the pigs and the herd of about two thousand rushed down the steep bank into the sea and drowned in the water
verses.literalPt: Ele o permitiu. Eles, saindo, entraram nos porcos; a manada, que era cerca de dois mil, precipitou-se pelo declive no mar, e ali se afogaram.

verses.original: Καὶ οἱ βόσκοντες αὐτοὺς ἔφυγον καὶ ἀπήγγειλαν εἰς τὴν πόλιν καὶ εἰς τοὺς ἀγρούς καὶ ἦλθον ἰδεῖν τί ἐστιν τὸ γεγονός
verses.transliteration: Kai hoi boskontes autous ephygon kai apēngeilan eis tēn polin kai eis tous agrous kai ēlthon idein ti estin to gegonos
verses.literal: Those tending the pigs ran off and reported this in the town and - countryside and the people went out to see what had happened
verses.literalPt: Os pastores fugiram e foram dar notícia disso na cidade e nos campos; e muitos foram ver o que tinha acontecido.

verses.original: καὶ ἔρχονται πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ θεωροῦσιν τὸν δαιμονιζόμενον καθήμενον ἱματισμένον καὶ σωφρονοῦντα τὸν ἐσχηκότα τὸν λεγιῶνα καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν
verses.transliteration: kai erchontai pros ton Iēsoun kai theōrousin ton daimonizomenon kathēmenon himatismenon kai sōphronounta ton eschēkota ton legiōna kai ephobēthēsan
verses.literal: When they came to Jesus they saw the man who had been possessed - by the legion of demons sitting there clothed and in his right mind and they were afraid
verses.literalPt: Chegando-se a Jesus, viram o endemoninhado que havia tido a legião, sentado, vestido e em perfeito juízo; e ficaram com medo.

verses.original: καὶ διηγήσαντο αὐτοῖς οἱ ἰδόντες πῶς ἐγένετο τῷ δαιμονιζομένῳ καὶ περὶ τῶν χοίρων
verses.transliteration: kai diēgēsanto autois hoi idontes pōs egeneto tō daimonizomenō kai peri tōn choirōn
verses.literal: Those who had seen it described . . . what had happened to the demon-possessed man and also to the pigs
verses.literalPt: Os que presenciaram o fato contaram-lhes o que havia acontecido ao endemoninhado e aos porcos.

verses.original: καὶ ἤρξαντο παρακαλεῖν αὐτὸν ἀπελθεῖν ἀπὸ τῶν ὁρίων αὐτῶν
verses.transliteration: kai ērxanto parakalein auton apelthein apo tōn horiōn autōn
verses.literal: And the people began to beg Jesus to leave . . . their region
verses.literalPt: Começaram a rogar-lhe que se retirasse daqueles termos.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐμβαίνοντος αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸ πλοῖον παρεκάλει αὐτὸν ὁ δαιμονισθεὶς ἵνα μετ’ αὐτοῦ ᾖ
verses.transliteration: Kai embainontos autou eis to ploion parekalei auton ho daimonistheis hina met’ autou ē
verses.literal: As He was getting into the boat the man who had been possessed by the demons begged to go with Him
verses.literalPt: Ao entrar ele na barca, aquele que fora endemoninhado rogou-lhe que o deixasse estar com ele.

verses.original: καὶ οὐκ ἀφῆκεν αὐτόν ἀλλὰ λέγει αὐτῷ Ὕπαγε εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου πρὸς τοὺς σούς καὶ ἀπάγγειλον αὐτοῖς ὅσα ὁ Κύριός σοι πεποίηκεν καὶ ἠλέησέν σε
verses.transliteration: kai ouk aphēken auton alla legei autō Hypage eis ton oikon sou pros tous sous kai apangeilon autois hosa ho Kyrios soi pepoiēken kai ēleēsen se
verses.literal: But Jesus would not allow him Go home . . . to your own people He said and tell them how much the Lord has done for you and what mercy He has shown you
verses.literalPt: Jesus não o permitiu, mas disse-lhe: Vai para tua casa, para teus parentes, e conta-lhes tudo o que o Senhor te fez e como teve compaixão de ti.

verses.original: Καὶ ἀπῆλθεν καὶ ἤρξατο κηρύσσειν ἐν τῇ Δεκαπόλει ὅσα ἐποίησεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ πάντες ἐθαύμαζον
verses.transliteration: Kai apēlthen kai ērxato kēryssein en tē Dekapolei hosa epoiēsen autō ho Iēsous kai pantes ethaumazon
verses.literal: So the man went away and began to proclaim throughout the Decapolis how much Jesus had done for him And everyone was amazed
verses.literalPt: Retirando-se, começou a publicar em Decápolis tudo o que lhe havia feito Jesus; e todos ficaram maravilhados.

verses.original: Καὶ διαπεράσαντος τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ πάλιν εἰς τὸ πέραν συνήχθη ὄχλος πολὺς ἐπ’ αὐτόν καὶ ἦν παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν
verses.transliteration: Kai diaperasantos tou Iēsou en tō ploiō palin eis to peran synēchthē ochlos polys ep’ auton kai ēn para tēn thalassan
verses.literal: When Jesus had again crossed . . . by boat to the other side a large crowd gathered around Him - beside the sea
verses.literalPt: Tendo Jesus voltado na barca para o outro lado, afluiu para ele uma grande multidão; e ele estava à beira do mar.

verses.original: καὶ ἔρχεται εἷς τῶν ἀρχισυναγώγων ὀνόματι Ἰάϊρος καὶ ἰδὼν αὐτὸν πίπτει πρὸς τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: kai erchetai heis tōn archisynagōgōn onomati Iairos kai idōn auton piptei pros tous podas autou
verses.literal: A synagogue leader named Jairus arrived and seeing Jesus he fell at His feet
verses.literalPt: Chegou-se a ele um dos chefes da sinagoga, chamado Jairo; vendo-o, lançou-se-lhe aos pés

verses.original: καὶ παρακαλεῖ αὐτὸν πολλὰ λέγων ὅτι Τὸ θυγάτριόν μου ἐσχάτως ἔχει ἵνα ἐλθὼν ἐπιθῇς τὰς χεῖρας αὐτῇ ἵνα σωθῇ καὶ ζήσῃ
verses.transliteration: kai parakalei auton polla legōn hoti To thygatrion mou eschatōs echei hina elthōn epithēs tas cheiras autē hina sōthē kai zēsē
verses.literal: and pleaded with Him urgently - My little daughter is near death Please come and place Your hands on her so that she will be healed and live
verses.literalPt: e rogou-lhe com instância, dizendo: Minha filhinha está a expirar; suplico-te que venhas pôr as mãos sobre ela, para que sare e viva.

verses.original: Καὶ ἀπῆλθεν μετ’ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ ὄχλος πολύς καὶ συνέθλιβον αὐτόν
verses.transliteration: Kai apēlthen met’ autou kai ēkolouthei autō ochlos polys kai synethlibon auton
verses.literal: So Jesus went with him and a large crowd followed and pressed around Him
verses.literalPt: Jesus foi com ele, e uma grande multidão, seguindo-o, o apertava.

verses.original: Καὶ γυνὴ οὖσα ἐν ῥύσει αἵματος δώδεκα ἔτη
verses.transliteration: Kai gynē ousa en rhysei haimatos dōdeka etē
verses.literal: And a woman was there who had suffered from bleeding for twelve years
verses.literalPt: Ora uma, mulher, que durante doze anos padecia de uma hemorragia,

verses.original: καὶ πολλὰ παθοῦσα ὑπὸ πολλῶν ἰατρῶν καὶ δαπανήσασα τὰ παρ’ αὐτῆς πάντα καὶ μηδὲν ὠφεληθεῖσα ἀλλὰ μᾶλλον εἰς τὸ χεῖρον ἐλθοῦσα
verses.transliteration: kai polla pathousa hypo pollōn iatrōn kai dapanēsasa ta par’ autēs panta kai mēden ōphelētheisa alla mallon eis to cheiron elthousa
verses.literal: She had borne much agony under the care of many physicians and had spent all she had but to no avail Instead her condition had only grown worse
verses.literalPt: e que tinha sofrido bastante às mãos de muitos médicos, e gastado tudo quanto possuía, sem nada aproveitar, antes, ficando cada vez pior,

verses.original: ἀκούσασα τὰ περὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἐλθοῦσα ἐν τῷ ὄχλῳ ὄπισθεν ἥψατο τοῦ ἱματίου αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: akousasa ta peri tou Iēsou elthousa en tō ochlō opisthen hēpsato tou himatiou autou
verses.literal: When the woman heard about Jesus she came up through the crowd behind Him and touched His cloak
verses.literalPt: tendo ouvido falar a respeito de Jesus, veio por detrás, entre a multidão, e tocou-lhe a capa;

verses.original: ἔλεγεν γὰρ ὅτι Ἐὰν ἅψωμαι κἂν τῶν ἱματίων αὐτοῦ σωθήσομαι
verses.transliteration: elegen gar hoti Ean hapsōmai kan tōn himatiōn autou sōthēsomai
verses.literal: For she kept saying If only I touch . . . His garments I will be healed
verses.literalPt: porque dizia: Se eu tocar somente as suas vestes, ficarei curada.

verses.original: καὶ εὐθὺς ἐξηράνθη ἡ πηγὴ τοῦ αἵματος αὐτῆς καὶ ἔγνω τῷ σώματι ὅτι ἴαται ἀπὸ τῆς μάστιγος
verses.transliteration: kai euthys exēranthē hē pēgē tou haimatos autēs kai egnō tō sōmati hoti iatai apo tēs mastigos
verses.literal: Immediately her bleeding stopped and she sensed in her body that she was healed of her affliction
verses.literalPt: No mesmo instante, cessou a sua hemorragia, e sentiu no seu corpo que estava curada do seu flagelo.

verses.original: Καὶ εὐθὺς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐπιγνοὺς ἐν ἑαυτῷ τὴν ἐξ αὐτοῦ δύναμιν ἐξελθοῦσαν ἐπιστραφεὶς ἐν τῷ ὄχλῳ ἔλεγεν Τίς μου ἥψατο τῶν ἱματίων
verses.transliteration: Kai euthys ho Iēsous epignous en heautō tēn ex autou dynamin exelthousan epistrapheis en tō ochlō elegen Tis mou hēpsato tōn himatiōn
verses.literal: At once Jesus was aware . . . . . . that power had gone out from Him Turning to the crowd He asked Who touched My garments
verses.literalPt: Jesus, conhecendo logo por si mesmo a virtude que dele saíra, virando-se no meio da multidão, perguntou: Quem tocou as minhas vestes?

verses.original: Καὶ ἔλεγον αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ Βλέπεις τὸν ὄχλον συνθλίβοντά σε καὶ λέγεις Τίς μου ἥψατο
verses.transliteration: Kai elegon autō hoi mathētai autou Blepeis ton ochlon synthlibonta se kai legeis Tis mou hēpsato
verses.literal: His disciples answered You can see the crowd pressing in on You and yet You ask Who touched Me
verses.literalPt: Responderam-lhe seus discípulos: Vês que a multidão te aperta e perguntas: Quem me tocou?

verses.original: Καὶ περιεβλέπετο ἰδεῖν τὴν τοῦτο ποιήσασαν
verses.transliteration: Kai perieblepeto idein tēn touto poiēsasan
verses.literal: But He kept looking around to see who had done this
verses.literalPt: Mas ele olhava ao redor para ver a que isso fizera.

verses.original: ἡ δὲ γυνὴ φοβηθεῖσα καὶ τρέμουσα εἰδυῖα ὃ γέγονεν αὐτῇ ἦλθεν καὶ προσέπεσεν αὐτῷ καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ πᾶσαν τὴν ἀλήθειαν
verses.transliteration: hē de gynē phobētheisa kai tremousa eiduia ho gegonen autē ēlthen kai prosepesen autō kai eipen autō pasan tēn alētheian
verses.literal: Then the woman knowing what had happened to her came and fell down before Him trembling in fear and she told Him the whole truth
verses.literalPt: A mulher, receosa e trêmula, cônscia do que nela se havia operado, veio, prostrou-se diante dele e declarou-lhe toda a verdade.

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῇ Θυγάτηρ ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε ὕπαγε εἰς εἰρήνην καὶ ἴσθι ὑγιὴς ἀπὸ τῆς μάστιγός σου
verses.transliteration: Ho de eipen autē Thygatēr hē pistis sou sesōken se hypage eis eirēnēn kai isthi hygiēs apo tēs mastigos sou
verses.literal: Daughter - said Jesus your faith has healed you Go in peace and be free of your affliction
verses.literalPt: Jesus disse-lhe: Filha, a tua fé te curou; vai-te em paz e fica livre do teu mal.

verses.original: Ἔτι αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος ἔρχονται ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀρχισυναγώγου λέγοντες ὅτι Ἡ θυγάτηρ σου ἀπέθανεν τί ἔτι σκύλλεις τὸν διδάσκαλον
verses.transliteration: Eti autou lalountos erchontai apo tou archisynagōgou legontes hoti Hē thygatēr sou apethanen ti eti skylleis ton didaskalon
verses.literal: While He was still speaking messengers from the house of Jairus arrived and said Your daughter is dead why bother the Teacher anymore
verses.literalPt: Ele ainda falava, quando vieram pessoas da casa do chefe da sinagoga, dizendo a este: Tua filha já morreu; por que incomodas mais o Mestre?

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς παρακούσας τὸν λόγον λαλούμενον λέγει τῷ ἀρχισυναγώγῳ Μὴ φοβοῦ μόνον πίστευε
verses.transliteration: Ho de Iēsous parakousas ton logon laloumenon legei tō archisynagōgō Mē phobou monon pisteue
verses.literal: But Jesus overheard their conversation and said to Jairus Do not be afraid just believe
verses.literalPt: Jesus, sem atender a essas palavras, disse ao chefe da sinagoga: Não temas, crê somente.

verses.original: καὶ οὐκ ἀφῆκεν οὐδένα μετ’ αὐτοῦ συνακολουθῆσαι εἰ μὴ τὸν Πέτρον καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ Ἰωάννην τὸν ἀδελφὸν Ἰακώβου
verses.transliteration: kai ouk aphēken oudena met’ autou synakolouthēsai ei mē ton Petron kai Iakōbon kai Iōannēn ton adelphon Iakōbou
verses.literal: And He did not allow anyone to accompany . . . Him except . . . Peter James and John the brother of James
verses.literalPt: Não permitiu que ninguém o acompanhasse, senão Pedro, Tiago e João, irmão de Tiago.

verses.original: Καὶ ἔρχονται εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ ἀρχισυναγώγου καὶ θεωρεῖ θόρυβον καὶ κλαίοντας καὶ ἀλαλάζοντας πολλά
verses.transliteration: Kai erchontai eis ton oikon tou archisynagōgou kai theōrei thorybon kai klaiontas kai alalazontas polla
verses.literal: When they arrived at the house of the synagogue leader Jesus saw the commotion and the people weeping and wailing loudly
verses.literalPt: Tendo eles chegado à casa do chefe da sinagoga, viu Jesus um alvoroço e os que choravam e faziam grande pranto;

verses.original: καὶ εἰσελθὼν λέγει αὐτοῖς Τί θορυβεῖσθε καὶ κλαίετε τὸ παιδίον οὐκ ἀπέθανεν ἀλλὰ καθεύδει
verses.transliteration: kai eiselthōn legei autois Ti thorybeisthe kai klaiete to paidion ouk apethanen alla katheudei
verses.literal: He went inside and asked Why all this commotion and weeping The child is not dead but asleep
verses.literalPt: e, tendo entrado, disse-lhes: Por que fazeis alvoroço e chorais? A menina não está morta, mas sim dormindo.

verses.original: καὶ κατεγέλων αὐτοῦ Αὐτὸς δὲ ἐκβαλὼν πάντας παραλαμβάνει τὸν πατέρα τοῦ παιδίου καὶ τὴν μητέρα καὶ τοὺς μετ’ αὐτοῦ καὶ εἰσπορεύεται ὅπου ἦν τὸ παιδίον
verses.transliteration: kai kategelōn autou Autos de ekbalōn pantas paralambanei ton patera tou paidiou kai tēn mētera kai tous met’ autou kai eisporeuetai hopou ēn to paidion
verses.literal: And they laughed at Him After He had put them all outside He took the child’s father and mother and His own companions . . . . . . and went in to see the child
verses.literalPt: Riam-se dele. Tendo, porém, feito sair a todos, ele tomou consigo o pai, e a mãe da menina, e os que com ele vieram e entrou onde estava a menina.

verses.original: καὶ κρατήσας τῆς χειρὸς τοῦ παιδίου λέγει αὐτῇ Ταλιθὰ κούμ ὅ ἐστιν μεθερμηνευόμενον Τὸ Κοράσιον σοὶ λέγω ἔγειρε
verses.transliteration: kai kratēsas tēs cheiros tou paidiou legei autē Talitha koum ho estin methermēneuomenon To Korasion soi legō egeire
verses.literal: Taking her by the hand Jesus said Talitha koum which means Little girl I say to you get up
verses.literalPt: Tomando-a pela mão, disse-lhe: Talita cumi, que quer dizer Menina, eu te digo: levanta-te.

verses.original: καὶ εὐθὺς ἀνέστη τὸ κοράσιον καὶ περιεπάτει ἦν γὰρ ἐτῶν δώδεκα καὶ ἐξέστησαν εὐθὺς ἐκστάσει μεγάλῃ
verses.transliteration: kai euthys anestē to korasion kai periepatei ēn gar etōn dōdeka kai exestēsan euthys ekstasei megalē
verses.literal: Immediately the girl got up and began to walk around she was twelve years old And at once they were utterly astounded . . . . . .
verses.literalPt: Imediatamente, ela se levantou e começou a andar, pois tinha doze anos. Então, eles ficaram sobremaneira admirados.

verses.original: καὶ διεστείλατο αὐτοῖς πολλὰ ἵνα μηδεὶς γνοῖ τοῦτο καὶ εἶπεν δοθῆναι αὐτῇ φαγεῖν
verses.transliteration: kai diesteilato autois polla hina mēdeis gnoi touto kai eipen dothēnai autē phagein
verses.literal: Then Jesus gave strict orders . . . . . . that no one should know about this and He told them to give her something to eat
verses.literalPt: Jesus recomendou-lhes expressamente que ninguém o soubesse e mandou que lhe dessem a ela de comer.
